record.original_question: Given a finite numerical sequence {f_k}_{k=0}^n, define the polynomial P_n(z) by P_n(z) = sum_{k=0}^n f_k f_{n-k} binom(n,k) [(z)_k (z)_{n-k} - (z+1)_k (z-1)_{n-k}], where (z)_k is the Pochhammer symbol. If the generating polynomial sum_{k=0}^n f_k z^k has only real negative zeros, must the polynomial P_n(z) also have only real negative zeros?

evidence.quote: For a given finite numerical sequence {fk}_k=0^n define the polynomial Pn(z) by Pn(z)=sum_{k=0}^n fk f_{n-k} binom(n,k) [(z)_k (z)_{n-k} - (z + 1)_k (z - 1)_{n-k}], where (z)_0 = 1, (z)_k = z(z + 1) ... (z + k - 1), k >= 1, is the Pochhammer symbol.
Conjecture 1. Suppose the polynomial sum_{k=0}^n fk z^k has only real negative zeros. Then the same is true for the polynomial Pn(z) defined above.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a nonnegative integer $k$, let $(z)_0 = 1$ and $(z)_k = z(z+1)(z+2)\cdots(z+k-1)$ for $k \ge 1$ denote the (rising) Pochhammer symbol. Given a finite sequence of real numbers $\{f_k\}_{k=0}^n$, define the polynomial
$$P_n(z) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{n} f_k\, f_{n-k}\, \binom{n}{k}\, \Bigl[(z)_k\,(z)_{n-k} \;-\; (z+1)_k\,(z-1)_{n-k}\Bigr].$$
Suppose that the generating polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^{n} f_k z^k$ has only real, strictly negative zeros. Prove or disprove: under this hypothesis, the polynomial $P_n(z)$ also has only real, strictly negative zeros.
